title: Sleepy Words: The Origin of 'Salary' — Salt Money in Ancient Rome

seo.description:
Fall asleep to the origin of the word 'salary.' From Latin 'salarium' — salt money. Roman soldiers were paid in salt.

This is why we say someone is 'worth their salt.' This is why we say 'salad' — from Latin 'salata,' salted things.

The word travels through time, carrying the story of Roman commerce in its syllables.

Sleep well.

sections.title: The Word
sections.content: Salary. A fixed regular payment, typically paid on a monthly or biweekly basis.

sections.title: The Origin
sections.content: But the word is older than that. Much older. From Latin 'salarium.' Salt money.

sections.title: The Story
sections.content: In ancient Rome, soldiers were paid in salt. Salt was currency. Salt was wealth.

sections.title: The Journey
sections.content: The word traveled through Old French. Into Middle English. Into our mouths today.

sections.title: The Relatives
sections.content: This is why we say someone is 'worth their salt.' And 'salad' — from Latin 'salata,' salted things.

sections.title: Closing
sections.content: Every time you say 'salary,' you're speaking Latin. Sleep well.
